newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Sejm approves funds law, NFI tax break.
newsitem.headline: Polish Sejm approves funds law, NFI tax break.

text.p: Poland's Sejm, the lower house, approved on Thursday a bill on investment funds which includes a tax exemption on capital gains for National Investment Funds (NFIs), the Sejm speaker said.
Deputies voted 331 to two with seven abstentions in favour of the bill which creates a legal framework for all types of funds.
Among the bill's provisions is one that offers the 15 NFIs an income tax exemption for capital gains made on sales of firms in their portfolios.
The exemption applies only to sales of shares in companies contributed by the state treasury to the NFI programme.

In April the finance ministry announced that from the start of 1998 it would scrap a tax exemption for the 15 NFIs on gains made on sales of firms from their portfolios but later the investment-fund draft was amended to extend the exemption.
The debate on the issue kept trade in NFI units volatile last month and expectations of a final decision on the issue have kept NFI trade active this week, traders said.
The Sejm also decided to back the government's proposal to scrap a provision which allowed investment fund companies to run pension funds.

The government has argued that pension funds should be regulated solely by a special bill passed by the Sejm on Wednesday which introduces stringent safety provisions designed specifically for pension funds.
The bill has yet to clear the Senate and be signed by the president to become law.
